LESSON: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.5: Listening for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening for Information, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 7 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: how leisure time should be used. How can we extract specific information from a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an audio recording of activities carried out for fun and enjoyment,

2. work with peers to identify various activities taken up for fun and enjoyment,

3. collaborate with peers to answer direct and inferential questions on the recording,

4. play a language game involving the use of verbal instructions e.g. the ‘Simon says’ language game,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an audio recording of activities carried out for fun and enjoyment,
2. work with peers to identify various activities taken up for fun and enjoyment,
3. collaborate with peers to answer direct and inferential questions on the recording,
4. play a language game involving the use of verbal instructions e.g. the ‘Simon says’ language game,
5. engage in a dialogue with peers on

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: Interpersonal skills are enhanced as the learner engages in a dialogue about leisure time

in groups.

• Social Justice: This is enhanced as the learner allows peers an equal chance when collaborating to answer direct and

inferential questions on the recording.

Values:
Respect: This is promoted as the learner shows positive regard for self and others while playing a language game involving the

use of verbal instructions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with peers to share ideas on how leisure time should be used constructively.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of constructive use of leisure time to similar concepts in Religious Education.
